To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the salient meaning of a metaphor is always activated first at the lexical access level and (2) the context can facilitate or suppress the activation of the salient meaning at a later stage.

the N400 elicited in response to a metaphor was not affected by the preceding context, while the N4OO elicited in response in response to a Probe word was larger in response to a literal context compared with the metaphorical context, and the N400 in response to the Probe word was smaller in response to a target word preceded by a metaphorical context than a literal context.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
context is not always a determinant of metaphor processing.
the GSH model is a valid model for metaphor comprehension, and the context effect is a separate process from the salient meaning activation.
the salient literal meaning is processed first, but it can be either facilitated or suppressed depending on the context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the GSH model should be revised in the way that it is not the salience of the meaning itself that determines the precedence of semantic activation, but it is the salience of meaning in the given context.
the salient interpretation of metaphor is always processed first, but the nonsalient interpretation can also be accessed if the context is available.
salience is the primary factor determining lexical access, but context is a secondary factor determining meaning integration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metaphor comprehension is a dynamic process involving two stages, with the first stage being lexical access and the second stage being semantic integration.
context does play a significant role in metaphor processing.
context can influence metaphor interpretation, but it does not affect the order in which different meanings of a polysemous word get accessed.
